sentences.text:
Order 
This appeal is filed by the State.
On 05/03/2002, leave to appeal is granted and on 14/05/2002 it was directed that respondent shall appear before the A.S.J., Panna.
Now a PUD received from Special Judge (SC/ST) Act, District Panna informing that respondent/accused is not appearing before the Court from 15/06/2020.
As original record is received, heard on admission.

This appeal is filed being aggrieved of the judgment dated 20/01/2001 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Panna in Criminal Appeal No.37/2000, whereby acquitting the respondent from the charges punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(1) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

The appeal is filed on the following grounds:-
(i) that the Court below failed to see that the respondent is a shop keeper/kirana merchant.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:607 2 CRA-418-2002 The State Of M.P. vs Ramesh Sahu on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70894695/
1 (ii) that the Court below has not appreciated the material available on record in it true perspective.

sentences.text: (iii) that the findings and conclusions drawn by the Court below are perverse and hence, liable to be set aside.

(iv) that the prosecution case has not supported by the independent witnesses.
(v) that that the Food Inspector received the Public Analysis Report on 21/05/1996 and thereafter he filed a complaint before the trial Court on 27/01/1997.
The allegation against the accused/respondent is that Iodized Salt with brand name Sona Iodized may be adulterated therefore, 500 grams salt was purchased and the same was sampled as per rules.
The sampled salt was send for analysis and, thereafter, the report of Public Analysis was received that it was adulterated.
Hence, charge-sheet was filed against him.
On an appeal, it was found that witness Raj Govind did not support the statement of Food Inspector and he was declared hostile.
There was only one punch witness.

As mentioned in Para-11 of the judgment when the Public Analysis report was received on 21/05/1996, the complaint was filed on 27/01/1997 i.e. after the period of one year and there was no explanation was given.

Neither the trial Court considered this point because filing of complaint belatedly effects the right of the accused to request the Court to send second sample for public analysis and this in its a sufficient reason to allow the appeal of the accused.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:607 3 CRA-418-2002
In view of the aforesaid, it is seen that learned appellate Court in its judgment dated 20/01/2001 has considered all the factual and legal grounds.
Therefore, there is no reason to admit this appeal.
Accordingly, it is dismissed on admission stage itself.
(AVANINDRA KUMAR SINGH) JUDGE mc The State Of M.P. vs Ramesh Sahu on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70894695/
